tool.name: SpatiallyBalancedSample

summary.para: Selects a spatially balanced probability sample from a point, polyline, or polygon frame using the generalized random-tessellation stratified (GRTS) design of Stevens and Olsen (2004) -- the standard of large environmental monitoring programs, as implemented in the spsurvey R package. Every location keeps its full, known inclusion probability (design-based inference intact), while each realized draw spreads over the frame the way pure randomness only promises on average. Supports stratification, unequal (PPS) probability from a weight field, legacy sites, a minimum distance between sites, and ordered replacement sites: the output is written in reverse hierarchical order, so any leading run of SiteIDs is itself a spatially balanced sample. Design weights ride along for Horvitz-Thompson estimation. Works at every license level.

tool.usage:
Answers the survey-design question that follows "how many sites?": where should they go, so that the sample can speak for the whole frame? A simple random sample keeps its promises only on average -- any single draw can leave voids and clumps, wasting samples on autocorrelated neighbors while whole regions go unvisited. The GRTS design keeps the promises draw by draw: a hierarchical randomization (recursive quadrants in random order) maps the frame onto a line while preserving spatial proximity, and a systematic pass with a random start selects the sites. Every individual location is exactly as likely to be chosen as under a simple random sample, so the estimates remain unbiased and the inference remains sound; what changes is only WHICH COMBINATIONS of locations can turn up together in one draw -- the combinations that clump in one corner and ignore the rest can no longer occur. Stratified sampling restricts randomness in just the same way, and for the same reason.
The frame is a point feature class (each point a sampling unit -- lakes, patches, candidate stations), a polyline feature class (sites placed along the lines), or a polygon feature class (sites placed within the polygons; holes respected) -- the spsurvey package's three resource types exactly. Selections are honored. Geographic (latitude/longitude) frames are handled in an automatic Lambert azimuthal equal-area working projection -- a happy pairing, since equal-area treatment is precisely what areal inclusion probabilities require -- and written back in the input coordinate system.
Replacement sites and the SiteID order. Field sites prove inaccessible -- landowners decline, roads wash out. Ask for replacement sites and they are drawn in the SAME design, and the whole output is written in reverse hierarchical order (Stevens and Olsen 2004): any leading run of SiteIDs is itself a spatially balanced sample, so when a base site cannot be visited you take the next Site_Use = Over site in SiteID order and balance is preserved as far as possible. The larger the replacement pool relative to the base, the more the base sample's balance dilutes -- ask for a realistic reserve, not a bottomless one.
Stratification uses a stratum field; each stratum is sampled independently, with the total allocated proportionally to stratum area/length/count (exact largest-remainder apportionment) or equally. Unequal (PPS) probability (point frames) scales each unit's inclusion probability to a weight field -- sample large lakes more often than small ones -- with certainty units (probability 1) handled exactly. Legacy sites (point frames) are existing monitoring sites that must remain in the new sample: they are guaranteed selection and counted inside the base sample, per Dumelle et al. (2023). A minimum distance between base sites is honored by redrawing the design (spatial balance already discourages close pairs); when it cannot be fully met the tool keeps the best draw and says so plainly.
The report prints per-stratum counts and each stratum's spatial balance -- Var(v) and the Pielou evenness loss, computed from Voronoi cells of the base sites exactly as Stevens and Olsen (2004) define it (0 = perfectly balanced; simple random samples typically score 2-3 times worse). The whole-sample Var(v) and Pielou loss are also returned as derived outputs for ModelBuilder and scripting, alongside the total number of sites written. The output carries SiteID (the visit/replacement order), Site_Use (Legacy / Base / Over), Stratum, Design_Wgt (1 / inclusion probability -- the Horvitz-Thompson design weight), and Src_FID for point frames.
Relation to Esri's tools. Esri's Create Spatially Balanced Points implements the raster-based RRQRR variant of this idea (Theobald et al. 2007) and requires the Geostatistical Analyst extension (or an Advanced license); it takes inclusion-probability rasters and does not offer polyline frames or the ordered replacement contract. This tool implements the original vector GRTS design at every license level. For unconstrained random points with spacing and boundary options, see the Random Point Generator; for whole sampling arrays, the Random Sample Array Generator; for the balanced-acceptance alternative to GRTS see Robertson et al. (2013).
The random seed makes the design exactly reproducible -- cite it in a methods section.

param.name: in_frame
param.displayname: Sampling frame (points, polylines, or polygons; a layer's selection is honored)

dialogReference.para: The sampling frame: a point feature class (each point a sampling unit), polylines (sites placed along the lines), or polygons (sites placed within; holes respected). A map layer's selection is honored.

param.name: n_base
param.displayname: Number of base sites (the sample size)

dialogReference.para: The number of sites in the base sample -- the design you intend to visit. Legacy sites count toward this number.

param.name: n_over
param.displayname: Number of replacement sites (optional; drawn in the same design and used in SiteID order)

dialogReference.para: Extra sites (Site_Use = Over) drawn in the same spatially balanced design, for use when base sites prove inaccessible -- take them in SiteID order. A realistic reserve preserves balance better than a bottomless one.

param.name: stratum_field
param.displayname: Stratum field (optional; each stratum is sampled independently)

dialogReference.para: An integer or text field whose values define strata; each stratum receives its own independent spatially balanced sample.

param.name: alloc_method
param.displayname: Allocation of sites across the strata

dialogReference.para: Proportional to stratum size: the base (and replacement) totals are split by stratum area, length, or unit count with exact largest-remainder apportionment. Equal count in each stratum: every stratum receives the stated numbers.

param.name: aux_field
param.displayname: Unequal probability (PPS) weight field (point frames only; optional)

dialogReference.para: Point frames: a non-negative numeric field; each unit's inclusion probability is made proportional to it (probability-proportional-to-size). Units whose scaled probability reaches 1 become certainties, handled exactly. The Design_Wgt field reflects the resulting probabilities.

param.name: legacy_sites
param.displayname: Legacy sites (point frames only; existing sites guaranteed into the sample; optional)

dialogReference.para: Existing monitoring sites that must remain in the new sample (they must coincide with frame points). They are guaranteed selection, labeled Site_Use = Legacy, and counted INSIDE the base sample size.

No two BASE sites closer than this, in the units below. Honored by redrawing the design (spatial balance already discourages close pairs); if it cannot be fully met after the retries, the tool keeps the best draw and reports the remaining close pairs.

param.name: max_tries
param.displayname: Selection retries to satisfy the minimum distance

dialogReference.para: Advanced: how many fresh designs to draw in search of one meeting the minimum distance (default 10). The best draw is kept either way.

param.name: random_seed
param.displayname: Random seed (optional -- same seed, same sites)

dialogReference.para: Optional: the same seed with the same inputs reproduces the same design exactly. Leave blank for a fresh draw each run.

The design sites, written in reverse hierarchical order: SiteID (visit/replacement order), Site_Use (Legacy / Base / Over), Stratum, Design_Wgt (1 / inclusion probability), and Src_FID for point frames.
The total number of design sites written (base + replacements), for ModelBuilder chains.

param.name: out_var_v
param.displayname: Spatial balance Var(v) of the base sites (derived; 0 = perfectly balanced)

dialogReference.para: The Voronoi-based spatial balance of the whole base sample, after Stevens and Olsen (2003): each site should claim an equal share of the frame (v = 1), and this is the variance of those shares. 0 is perfect balance; simple random samples typically run 2-3 times higher. Reported per stratum in the run messages; this value covers the whole sample, for ModelBuilder.

param.name: out_pielou
param.displayname: Pielou evenness loss of the base sites (derived; 0 = perfectly balanced)

dialogReference.para: A companion balance measure (Dumelle and colleagues): how far the sites' shares of the frame fall from perfect evenness, on a 0-1 scale where 0 is perfectly balanced. Covers the whole base sample, for ModelBuilder.

scriptExample.title: Spatially Balanced Sample (GRTS) example (stand-alone script)
scriptExample.para: A 50-site design over lake polygons with 10 ordered replacement sites, reproducible with a seed.
scriptExample.code: import arcpy arcpy.ImportToolbox(r"C:\path\to\JennessEnterprisesTools.pyt") # your install path # alloc_method options (matching is by prefix): # "Proportional to stratum size (area, length, or unit count)" # "Equal count in each stratum" # linear_units: "Meters" / "Kilometers" / "Feet" / "Miles" result = arcpy.jenness.SpatiallyBalancedSample( in_frame=r"D:\data\study.gdb\lakes", n_base=50, n_over=10, random_seed=42, out_fc=r"D:\data\study.gdb\lakes_GRTS") print(result.getOutput(1)) # total sites written print(result.getOutput(2)) # spatial balance Var(v), 0 = perfect print(result.getOutput(3)) # Pielou evenness loss, 0 = perfect
